summary: Chandradhar Sharma Guleri was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Allahabad (~1899–1903) and served as Head Pandit at Mayo College (~1904–1920) before holding a post at Banaras Hindu University (~1920–1922).

Chang-geun Hwang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2000. He studied under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, advisor Minoru Kiyota, and doctoral supervisor Morten Schlütter.

Changhwan Park is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University under Noritoshi Aramaki and Shoryu Katsura, and completed a PhD at UC Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt. He was a professor at Geumgang University (attested 2013–2017).

Changpei Luo was a linguistics and Sinology scholar who studied at Peking University (~1916–1921). He held posts at Northwest University (~1924–1926), Xiamen University (~1926–1927), Sun Yat-sen University (~1928–1929), and Peking University (~1934–1950).

Chanju Mun is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (2001–2002) and completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2002). His supervisors included Charles Hallisey, Morten Schlütter, and Masahiro Shimoda, alongside teacher John D. Dunne.

Channa Li is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She was a PhD candidate at Leiden University (attested 2019), having studied under Jonathan A. Silk (attested 2015), and is a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Chao-heng Liao is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held a post at Academia Sinica (attested 2018) and served as an adjunct researcher at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Charlene Makley is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Michigan in 1999 under Norma Diamond and Roy Rappaport, and has served as an associate professor of anthropology at Reed College.

Charles Alexander Moore was a philosopher who earned his AB and PhD from Yale University (~1922–1932), where he also taught (~1933–1936). He was a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1936–1967) and founded Philosophy East and West.
Charles Alfred Bell was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He completed his education at Winchester College (~1884–1889) and New College (~1889–1891).

Charles B. Jones is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He completed a PhD at the University of Virginia (1996) under Paul Groner and served as Associate Professor and Associate Dean at the Catholic University of America (attested 2016–2019).

Charles Bally was a linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1886–1889) and under Ferdinand de Saussure (~1893–1913). He held a post at the University of Geneva from approximately 1893 to 1939.

Charles Burnett is a scholar of history, archaeology, and philosophy who earned his BA and doctorate at the University of Cambridge (~1969–1976). He held positions at St John's College, the University of Sheffield, and the Warburg Institute, becoming professor there in 1999.

Charles Cutler Torrey was a scholar in religious studies, history/archaeology, and linguistics who studied under Theodor Nöldeke (~1891–1892). He taught Semitic languages at Andover Theological Seminary (1892–1900) and was a professor at Yale University (1900–1932).

Charles D. Orzech is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who completed his dissertation at the University of Chicago. He chaired the Religious Studies Department at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro (attested 1998–2006).

Charles DiSimone is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of Munich in 2016. He held a post at the University of Munich (attested 2021) and serves at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Charles Duroiselle was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Indology. He taught as a professor at the University of Rangoon and served as Superintendent of the Archaeological Survey of Burma (1912–1940) and Archaeological Survey of India Burma Circle.

Charles Edmund Godakumbura was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history/archaeology who earned multiple degrees, including a PhD and D.Litt., from the University of London. He taught at SOAS (~1953–1959) and served as Archaeological Commissioner (1956–1967).

Charles Eliot was a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied at Cheltenham College and Balliol College, Oxford. He served at the Foreign Office (~1886–1926), the University of Sheffield (~1905–1912), and as principal of the University of Hong Kong (~1912–1918).
Charles Elliott was active in Indology and other fields. He served in the East India Company (~1795–1827) and later served as Treasurer of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1836–1856).
